title: 水盆里的蓝墨水  (Floating in the Basin)

segments.t: By the carved stone water basin in the corner of the courtyard, Zhou holds up a dripping pale-blue sheet of paper while Chen hands him a dry cotton towel and Mei tries heroically not to laugh. Listen first.
你看第三桌——梧桐巷的街坊全晕成一只大蓝水母了！
老板，拿这条干毛巾擦擦袖子吧，好在盆里的水还算凉快。
说真的，周经理，现在咖啡馆里正流行这种抽象水彩画呢！
没有个像样的座位表，明天二十八位街坊怎么体面地入座呀？！
先定定神想想——每位街坊该坐哪儿，你脑子里还记得清清楚楚，对吧？
老陈，每个座位我当然记得，可户外桌子上的纸卡片一吹就跑啊！
老陈，他说得在理；连折好的纸名牌十分钟前都飞走了。
纸会飞走，只是因为没人把它夹在重东西上。
夹起来？用什么夹——难不成往干净白亚麻餐巾上压大铁马蹄铁？！
你就待在这儿喝五口薄荷茶，我去翻翻工具间的抽屉。
老陈，趁绳子还没打死结，先帮志豪把头顶缠住的灯笼解下来吧！
先救灯笼，再解决防风座位——有我在，谁都别慌。
Now let's go through it line by line with the English translation.
你看第三桌——梧桐巷的街坊全晕成一只大蓝水母了！

'Look at Table Three—everyone on Wutong Lane has bled together into one giant blue jellyfish!' "Yun cheng" describes ink bleeding and spreading into a new shape, and "shuimu" ("water mother") is the lovely Chinese word for jellyfish.
老板，拿这条干毛巾擦擦袖子吧，好在盆里的水还算凉快。

'Here's a dry towel to wipe your sleeves, boss; at least the water in the basin stayed cool.' "Haozai" brings silver-lining relief ("luckily" or "at least"), and doubling "ca" into "caca" suggests a quick wipe.
说真的，周经理，现在咖啡馆里正流行这种抽象水彩画呢！

'Honestly, Zhou, this kind of abstract watercolor art is super trendy in cafes right now!' "Shuo zhende" means "to tell the truth" or "seriously," while "shuicaihua" literally combines water ("shui"), color ("cai"), and painting ("hua").
没有个像样的座位表，明天二十八位街坊怎么体面地入座呀？！

'Without a proper seating chart, how can twenty-eight neighbors take their seats decently tomorrow?!' "Xiangyang" means "presentable" or "looking the part," and "ruzuo" is the polite, formal way to say "take one's seat."
先定定神想想——每位街坊该坐哪儿，你脑子里还记得清清楚楚，对吧？

'Steady yourself and think—you still remember clearly in your head where every neighbor belongs, right?' "Dingding shen" literally means "settle your spirit" (catch your breath), and doubled "qingqing chuchu" emphasizes crystal-clear memory.
老陈，每个座位我当然记得，可户外桌子上的纸卡片一吹就跑啊！

'Of course I remember every seat, Chen, yet paper cards on outdoor tables blow away in a snap!' Pairing "yi" and "jiu" ("yichui jiupao") literally marks instant cause and effect: the moment the wind blows, the cards take off.
老陈，他说得在理；连折好的纸名牌十分钟前都飞走了。

'He has a point, Chen; even the folded paper place cards blew away ten minutes ago.' "Shuo de zai li" means "what he says stands on reason" ("he has a point"), while "zhe hao" marks cards already folded and ready.
纸会飞走，只是因为没人把它夹在重东西上。
'Paper only flies away because nobody clipped it onto something heavy.' "Ba ta jia zai ..." puts the paper up front with "ba" so the focus lands cleanly on clipping it onto a weighty object.
夹起来？用什么夹——难不成往干净白亚麻餐巾上压大铁马蹄铁？！

'Clip it? With what—don't tell me we're weighting clean white linen napkins with heavy iron horseshoes?!' Incredulous "nanbucheng" asks "could it really be that...?" while "yama canjin" names woven linen table napkins.
你就待在这儿喝五口薄荷茶，我去翻翻工具间的抽屉。

'Stay right here, take five sips of mint tea, and let me rummage through my workshop drawer.' Individual sips take the counter "kou" ("wu kou bohe cha", five mouthfuls of mint tea), and "fanfan" means to flip or rummage through.
老陈，趁绳子还没打死结，先帮志豪把头顶缠住的灯笼解下来吧！

'Chen, before the cord ties into a dead knot, help Hao rescue those tangled lanterns overhead first!' A "sijie" ("dead knot") is a stubborn knot you can't pull loose, and "jie xialai" means to untangle and bring them down.
先救灯笼，再解决防风座位——有我在，谁都别慌。

'Rescue the lanterns first, solve the windproof seats second—with me here, nobody panic.' "Fangfeng" pairs "guard against" ("fang") + "wind" ("feng") to mean windproof, and "you wo zai" reassures everyone ("while I'm here").
Now let's listen to the whole conversation one last time.

While the blue ink jellyfish dries in the sun, Chen heads upstairs with a plan to outsmart the Friday wind. See you next time.
